features.title: OKLCH-native design token package
acceptance: design-system.manifest.json compiles to CSS custom properties, TypeScript, React Native styles and a Tailwind v4 theme

Every status token pairs with an icon token; a status expressible only as colour cannot be constructed

Gate 9 (contrast) activates, report-only while the manifest status is placeholder
features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: the manifest compiles to four targets (CSS custom properties with an @supports OKLCh upgrade, TypeScript constants, React Native styles, a Tailwind v4 theme), every output committed and BYTE-COMPARED by its tests; gate 9 (contrast) ACTIVE and BLOCKING after being watched fail on five real defects, with an eight-case mutation proof in CI (scripts/verify-contrast-proof.mjs) asserting the baseline green in each — seven that must go red, and one that must stay green (a placeholder manifest status with a real failure present, proving the report-only switch); the cvdPairs assertion in gate 10; the status/icon/text triple as a TYPE, so a colour-only status fails typecheck rather than review. THREE DEFECTS FOUND IN THE APPROVED MANIFEST: (1) 37 of 38 opaque tokens had an srgb hex that did not match their own oklch, up to 6.09 dE00 — settled by ADR-0043, srgb is now engine-derived and a hand-edited hex fails the gate; (2) a DUPLICATE JSON KEY meant the top-level "status": "approved" never survived parsing, so gate.contrast.blockingWhenStatus compared against an object and the gate could never block — the pairing block is renamed statusPairing; (3) five WCAG AA failures and five CVD separation failures in the approved values, corrected in ADR-0044, whose real content is the decision to classify status.* as usage:"text" (4.5:1) rather than nonText (3:1). NOT DELIVERED: the half of gate 9 that scans RENDERED surfaces for colour-only status indicators — no component exists until F-017, and the gate prints that on every run. THE COLOUR-SCIENCE REVIEW RETURNED CHANGES REQUIRED AND FOUND FOUR REAL DEFECTS IN THE GATE, ALL FIXED: (a) the comment justifying a single severity check was FALSE — Machado is not monotone, and light status.warn/status.bad under tritan scores 61.2 at severity 0.90 against 65.8 at 1.0, so all eleven tabulated severities are now checked; (b) the separation claim was model-dependent — under Vienot total dichromacy, which color-engine.md assigns to exactly this case, light status.ok/status.warn under protan scored 59.6, BELOW the declared 60, so both models are now checked and the worse taken, and the values moved again to clear it; (c) the alpha-compositing comment was factually INVERTED — for a light overlay on a dark ground the linear reading is 2.2x more PERMISSIVE, not stricter, and the encoded model is what browsers and React Native actually draw, so both are now computed and the worse taken; (d) gate coverage was driven entirely by pairsWith, so nine tokens per theme were checked by nothing while looking exactly like tokens that passed — a token covered by nothing now fails unless it declares an uncheckedReason. ALSO CORRECTED: a wrong unit in ADR-0044 (11/255 is the encoded byte, not the linear value), the chromaCeiling field name (surfaceAndText, when the rule had become universal, was an invitation to re-derive the exemption-by-classification bug from the field name), a missing Lab-illuminant statement on ADR-0043 dE00 column, and a factually wrong comment in packages/cvd-engine/src/machado.ts claiming every reference implementation applies the matrices in encoded sRGB — R colorspace and DaltonLens apply them in linear. The palette was recomputed under BOTH conventions and clears the minimum either way (61.9 linear, 64.0 encoded), which is now recorded there. INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED on the third evaluator attempt (the first two died on session limits). The evaluation reproduced every gate green and returned FAIL on the RECORD, which no gate reads: ADR-0044 value table showed the intermediate correction rather than what shipped, and DESIGN-SYSTEM.md claimed a TypeScript brand that no code applied — TextToken/LargeTextToken were phantom brands nothing produced. Both fixed; the types are now literal unions DERIVED from the manifest usage field. It also found that NOTHING isolated checkContrast: the one contrast mutation also broke the derived-hex check, so a checkContrast returning passes:true unconditionally left gate 9 exiting 0 and all eight mutations green — verified by neutering it. Now covered by test/check.test.ts and a ninth proof case. Also fixed: turbo.json gave test:contrast no dependency on its own build; the severity-sweep decoy matched rows scoring 100 at every severity; and six stale measurements including the record of a re-measurement that was not itself re-measured. NOT REVIEWED BY A HUMAN: the corrected palette was reviewed by the designer and colour-scientist subagents, not by the person who approved it; the manifest carries a valuesChangedSinceApproval field saying so, because status:approved is the one field a gate reads. All colour maths is delegated to @irodora/color-difference and @irodora/cvd-engine, so nothing here re-implements a metric. FOUND AND RECORDED RATHER THAN FIXED: F-067 (the two themes assert opposite salience hierarchies — pre-existing), F-068 (swatch edge against an arbitrary sample), F-069 (status colour adjacent to a sample). border.strong composited over a light surface reaches 1.17:1; it is in no pairsWith so nothing checks it, and that is recorded rather than silently widened.

features.title: Colour spaces and conversion
features.notes: The colour engine starts here. DELIVERED: eight spaces converting in both directions through XYZ D65, CAT16 and Bradford adaptation, five cited golden datasets (64 entries), 56 ordered round-trip pairs within ΔE00 0.01 over 10,000 stratified samples, oracle cross-validation against culori and colorjs.io — BITWISE identical to colorjs.io on XYZ, Lab-D65, P3 and linear sRGB — and gate 5 activated after each dataset was watched reject a real mutation. Zero runtime dependencies is now a CHECK (scripts/verify-engine-purity.mjs), not a claim: lint blocked node:* but nothing blocked `import chroma from 'chroma-js'`. ADR-0040 records the OKLab constants: CSS Color 4's recalculation rather than Ottosson's original ten decimals, which makes D65 white exactly neutral and this package bitwise identical to colorjs.io. ADR-0039 is its superseded predecessor, kept because its reasoning error — reading two oracles agreeing with each other as evidence about THEM — is the useful part. Criterion 5's Node leg and its whole mechanism are gated; the browser and React Native EXECUTIONS are attested (ADR-0038) — a browser ran the vectors once during this feature and matched the digest, but Chromium and Node are both V8, so that proves platform-API freedom rather than engine independence.

features.title: CVD engine and separation scoring
acceptance: Brettel-Vienot dichromacy and Machado anomalous trichromacy at severity 0 to 1
Dichromat simulation of a published confusion-line pair yields DeltaE00 below 2
One separation score in [0,100], combining post-simulation DeltaE00 with lightness difference, used identically by the UI and the recommendation engine
Gate 10 (cvd) activates
features.notes: IN PROGRESS. DELIVERED: Machado anomalous trichromacy for all three deficiencies across CONTINUOUS severity (culori snaps to 0.1 steps because its interpolation weight is Math.round(t % 0.1), always 0 — we interpolate, and the oracle is consulted only at the 11 tabulated points); Vienot dichromacy for protan and deutan; one separation score in [0,100] (E-005); gate 10 ACTIVE after being watched fail. NOT DELIVERED — acceptance criterion 1 is only partly met: TRITAN DICHROMACY. Vienot's single-plane simplification is not accurate for tritanopia, whose two half-planes diverge, so simulateDichromacy THROWS for it rather than returning a plausible wrong answer that would feed the separation score. The full two-half-plane Brettel 1997 construction is the remaining work, and there is no oracle for it in either library — the check will have to be the confusion-line property, as it is for the other two. THE BLOCKER IS IDENTIFIED AND PINNED: XYZ_TO_LMS_HPE is the WRONG fundamental set. A copunctal point is the chromaticity of the missing cone fundamental, so it is derivable from the LMS-to-XYZ columns; HPE gives tritan (0.1680, 0.0000) against the published (0.171, -0.003) — agreement to 0.003 — but protan (0.8374, 0.1626) against (0.747, 0.253) and deutan (2.3019, -1.3019) against (1.400, -0.400). The published points are Smith-Pokorny, which is also what Vienot derived from, so the remaining construction needs Smith-Pokorny fundamentals plus the four anchor stimuli (475/575 nm for protan and deutan, 485/660 nm for tritan). The fundamental set is now SETTLED: Smith-Pokorny reproduces all three published copunctal points (protan 0.0007, deutan 0.0002, tritan 0.0048). The ANCHOR STIMULI are the blocker, and an attempt was refuted rather than shipped: recalled anchors disagree with Vienot — which is the published single-plane reduction of Brettel, so a real oracle — by 32.5 dE00 (protan) and 57.4 (deutan), and the diagnostic explains why: the two half-plane normals sit 88.4 degrees apart where Vienot validity requires ~0. They cannot be derived here — computing LMS at a wavelength needs CIE colour-matching functions and there is NO spectral data in the dependency tree and no Brettel implementation to check against. FINISHING THIS NEEDS A DECISION, NOT CODE: vendor CIE colour-matching functions (a content and licensing question per content/AGENTS.md), obtain a trustworthy transcription of Brettel published anchor table, or attest criterion 1 under ADR-0038. Criterion 2 is met for protan and deutan using the kernel of the published Vienot matrix; note that pairs built from the classic published COPUNCTAL POINTS only collapse to ~5.2 dE00, because those points and Vienot's matrices come from different cone fundamentals. Recorded as a golden entry.

attested.criterion: Brettel-Vienot dichromacy and Machado anomalous trichromacy at severity 0 to 1
attested.verifiedBy: TRITAN DICHROMACY ONLY. Everything else in this criterion is gated: Machado anomalous trichromacy for all three deficiencies across continuous severity, and Vienot dichromacy for protan and deutan, are covered by gate 5 and gate 10 (ADR-0038 section 4 — where a part is checkable, that part stays gated). Tritan dichromacy needs the two-half-plane Brettel 1997 construction, which needs the LMS anchor stimuli at 485 and 660 nm. Those cannot be derived or verified here: computing LMS at a wavelength requires CIE colour-matching functions, there is no spectral data in the repository or its dependency tree, and neither culori nor colorjs.io implements Brettel. An attempt using recalled anchors was REFUTED and not shipped — it disagreed with Vienot (the published single-plane reduction of Brettel, and therefore a real oracle for protan and deutan) by 32.5 dE00 protan and 57.4 deutan, and the diagnostic showed the half-plane normals 88.4 degrees apart where Vienot validity requires ~0. DISCHARGED BY: implementing the construction against either vendored CIE colour-matching functions or a trustworthy transcription of Brettel published anchor table, and accepting only if BOTH checks pass — agreement with Vienot on protan and deutan, and near-coplanar half-plane normals. NOTE ON THE BAR: ADR-0038 asks for "verifying it requires a system we do not control". This is missing published source data rather than a missing system, which is a weaker case than a VPS or a physical device — recorded plainly rather than glossed. What makes it defensible is that tritan CVD is NOT unsupported: Machado tritanomaly is delivered across full severity and the separation score covers all three deficiencies through the Machado path, so only tritan DICHROMACY specifically is owed.

features.title: Gamut mapping
acceptance: Out-of-gamut colours map by OKLCh chroma reduction, preserving lightness and hue within stated bounds
Mapping an in-gamut colour is idempotent, asserted by property test
Golden set of known out-of-gamut colours and their mapped results
features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: gamutMap and gamutMapDetail in @irodora/color-spaces — OKLCh chroma bisection, 32 halvings, holding L and H, for sRGB and Display-P3. Zero new colour maths: every number is an existing engine conversion, and the feature is a search over a predicate. THE DECISION IS ADR-0045 AND IT IS A DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM CSS COLOR 4. The standard adds a MINDE early stop that returns the CLIPPED colour once it is within a JND in dEok, and dEok tolerates hue movement — measured against colorjs.io toGamut({method:css}) over 30 out-of-gamut colours, CSS drifts hue up to 11.97 degrees where we drift 2.6e-5, and the two results differ by up to 5.21 dE00. Our implementation was cross-checked against culori clampChroma, an independent implementation of the SAME algorithm: agreement 0.0063 dE00. The MINDE step was also structurally unavailable — dEok lives in @irodora/color-difference, which depends on this package, so implementing it would have meant a second implementation of a shipped function. Both reasons are recorded; the measurement is the one that decided it. THE STATED BOUND, which acceptance criterion 1 asks for: L and H are preserved EXACTLY in OKLCh (7e-12, the round-trip noise). After rendering, a final clamp of at most GAMUT_EPSILON=1e-7 per channel applies, and near the black point that tiny absolute movement is a large relative one — hue drift reaches 23 degrees below result L,C=0.01 where OKLCh hue is not a meaningful angle, and is 6.9e-5 degrees above L,C=0.05. Tabulated in the test rather than asserted at one convenient cutoff. THREE CASES ARE NOT CHROMA REDUCTION and each is an explicit branch: already in gamut (the early return is what makes idempotence exact), achromatic, and out of gamut in LIGHTNESS where no chroma fits and lightnessOutOfRange says so rather than a loop returning whatever it last held. THE DECOY is per-channel clipping — the algorithm almost everything else uses — implemented in the test and measured at 33.6 degrees of hue shift, with our own drift asserted beside it as the baseline. FOUND AND RECORDED, NOT FIXED: F-071, two pre-existing flaky property tests. oklab.test.ts round-trips 5000 unseeded fast-check samples against a 1e-12 bound and failed once during this feature at 1.2477e-12 before passing six consecutive full-suite runs; the F-003 evaluation found a second in packages/testing. A blocking gate that can go red for a reason unrelated to the change teaches people to re-run until green.

features.title: The Color value type and reproducibility envelope
acceptance: Color carries required Provenance; an unclassified colour is not constructible
Provenance records source, confidence, conditions and originSpace
Color.unsafeFromHex is the only untracked construction path, and every call site is reviewed
Every derived result carries {engine, corpus, rules, profile}
A regression test pins historical envelopes and replays them byte-identically
features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: the Color value type (canonical XYZ + required Provenance), fromXyz / fromSpace / unsafeFromHex / withProvenance, CaptureConditions, and the ReproducibilityEnvelope with a canonical serialisation and a historical replay fixture. No colour maths: this package is a facade and every conversion is @irodora/color-spaces. THE DESIGN DECISION: Provenance is a DISCRIMINATED UNION on source, not an interface with an optional conditions field. ADR-0005 says conditions is required when the source is estimated or calibrated, and an optional field only asks nicely — an estimate that lost its capture conditions would still compile, which is exactly the object nobody should be able to build. CaptureConditions was NOT invented for this: its fields are specified in docs/architecture/color-engine.md and match FR-17 (illuminant) and FR-18 (quality) exactly, so the union requires real data rather than an empty object. THE UNION BROKE THE WIRE PIN, AND THAT IS THE MECHANISM WORKING. ADR-0036 pins the engine type to the Zod schema at compile time; adding conditions turned it red immediately, which forced the contract to move in the same commit. But the union then WEAKENED the pin in a way that passed silently: keyof on a union returns only the keys COMMON to every member, so an optional field added to one member type-checked cleanly. Verified by doing it. The pin is now asserted PER MEMBER, and scripts/verify-contract-pin.mjs proves it — four probes, each adding an optional field to a different part of the schema, each asserted to turn typecheck red with the baseline asserted green first. EVERY CALL SITE IS REVIEWED, MADE COUNTABLE: scripts/verify-unsafe-call-sites.mjs enumerates unsafeFromHex call sites and runs inside pnpm lint; a new one fails the build until someone adds it to the reviewed list, which is the moment the review happens. It is a script rather than a test because the colour-engine ESLint zone forbids node: imports even in tests (NFR-3), and the alternative was weakening the strictest guard in the repository. THE REPLAY FIXTURE PINS HISTORICAL VERSIONS, not current ones, and asserts it: a fixture written from todays CORE_VERSION compares the code to itself and goes green for free. That assertion caught one of my own entries using 0.1.0.

attested.criterion: Five classifications enforced and displayed; our own curation cannot be marked historical
attested.verifiedBy: The colour-detail surface (F-018) rendering classification on every entry, asserted in its e2e and a11y run. The ENFORCED half is gated here — parseEntry rejects any other value and the mutation proof watches a japanese-inspired entry marked historical go red — but nothing in this repository can prove a field is DISPLAYED before a surface exists.

attested.criterion: Editorial workflow draft to review to verified to published to superseded; author and reviewer must differ
attested.verifiedBy: F-062 (editorial review workflow) driving an entry through the states with stored prior state, so a transition can be compared against one. The AUTHOR-AND-REVIEWER half is fully gated here and proven by three mutation cases (same id, same person under two ids, unknown id), as is every per-status obligation. The SEQUENCE half is not enforceable in a file-based corpus: nothing on disk records what status an entry held before this commit, so assertTransition has no caller and cannot have one until something stores that.

features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: the corpus schema as a parser (@irodora/corpus), the editorial workflow and identity rule, canonical JSON and the two-level checksum, the published-version bundle with verify-at-load, scripts/generate-corpus.mjs, and GATE 11 ACTIVE AND BLOCKING with a 19-case mutation proof. 211 tests. NO COLOUR WAS ADDED — content/colors/ is still empty, which is F-012. DERIVED VALUES ARE UNAUTHORABLE, not merely regenerated: parseEntry rejects lab, lch, oklch, rgb, hex and gamut BY NAME. That is one step stronger than ADR-0043, which must regenerate-and-compare because the design manifest keeps its srgb for browsers; nothing reads a hex out of a source entry, so the stronger form was available. The rejection points at color.sourceHex, because the spec section 1 example showed those keys and an editor would have copied it. THE GATE SHIPPED BEFORE ITS DATA, which is the hard part. F-011 builds the gate and F-012 supplies the entries, so on activation the corpus is EMPTY and a gate that passes over nothing is failing open for the whole of R1. Four answers: it FAILS if it cannot locate its inputs; it runs 1 valid + 18 invalid FIXTURE corpora every invocation so the rules exercised are never zero; the fixtures cannot become content (outside content/, the scan globs content/ only, and a fixture- slug under content/ is itself a failure); and verify-content-proof.mjs mutates the VALID corpus 19 ways asserting the gate goes red AND NAMES THE RIGHT FIELD, baseline green either side, with ONE case that must stay GREEN. The authored-entry count (0) prints beside the fixture count on every run. THE CI CONDITION WAS THE WHOLE BALLGAME: gate 11 step carried `if: hashFiles(content/colors) != ''`, and gate 0 compares `run:` commands without reading `if:` — so the gate would have been "active" and never once run in CI for the rest of R1, with nothing able to say so. Removed. The general case is F-072. THREE DOCUMENTS DISAGREED about required provenance: the spec section 1 list omitted sourceLicence, publisher, rightsHolder and editorialNotes; ADR-0007 section 1 requires them and NFR-20 names the licence. The accepted decision won and the spec was corrected. IDENTITY IS A ROSTER ID (ADR-0047) because the rule was UNENFORCEABLE — the schema had no author field at all, so "author and reviewer must differ" could not run. Free text would have passed "A. Ranjan" against "Ashish Ranjan", and an UNKNOWN id must FAIL rather than count as a third person, which is the half that matters. THE REGISTER CROSS-CHECK existed only as a sentence: licensing-and-provenance.md section 5 stated the content gate performs it. It did not. Now it does, and an unparseable table is a FAILURE rather than an absence of constraint. TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY TESTS DURING THE BUILD. (1) The per-entry checksum covered only the authored record, so a tampered derived hex LOADED CLEAN and apps/api would have served it (F-016); it now covers the derived block too. (2) The bundle serialised xyz as a tuple while parseEntry requires the authored {x,y,z}, so a bundle could not load its own output. AND TWO DEFECTS THE FIXTURES FOUND IN THEMSELVES: duplicate-slug was broken in two ways and failed for the wrong rule; then, filenames coming from slugs, both entries wrote to one file and it stopped being invalid at all. Both caught by the gate, not by review — which is the argument for generating fixtures rather than hand-maintaining eighteen copies. THE HUE BOUND WAS GUESSED AND WRONG. A CIELAB bound of 6 degrees for a gamut-mapped corpus hex failed at 7.97. Measured over the six Display-P3 corners: OKLCh drift ours 0.167 vs clipping 3.150; CIELAB ours 7.966 vs clipping 5.206. IN CIELAB CLIPPING LOOKS BETTER THAN WE DO — not an algorithm failure but CIELAB and OKLab disagreeing about hue exactly where the P3 primaries sit, which is why OKLab exists. gamutMap holds OKLCh hue by construction (ADR-0045), so OKLCh is the metric that describes it; the CIELAB row is asserted as a NON-claim, because picking the flattering ruler is the failure mode here. srgbToHex moved into @irodora/color-spaces and design-tokens.toHex delegates — proven safe by 96 design-tokens tests, gate 9 and all 9 contrast mutation proofs. E-001 DESTINATION HALF IS NOW GUARDED, which it has never been: the gate recomputes every derived value in the LATEST bundle under the CURRENT engine. Older versions are checksum-verified only and the gate PRINTS that it skipped them, because asserting today's engine reproduces yesterday's answer is the claim FR-10 forbids. EVALUATION FINDINGS, FIXED IN THE SAME FEATURE. (1) E-001's rationale claimed the mutation proof watched a perturbed OKLab matrix go red. IT DID NOT — there was no such case, and the evaluator ran the experiment and watched the gate stay green. The case now exists (rebuilds color-spaces and corpus, asserts gate 11 red, restores). (2) GATE 11'S ENTIRE PUBLISHED-BUNDLE BLOCK WAS UNREACHABLE: zero real bundles until F-012, no fixture carried one, and not one proof case touched a checksum — so the charter claimed checksum and E-001 destination enforcement by code that never ran. The valid fixture corpus now carries a published version and five proof cases attack it (edited entry, edited derived value, altered ledger checksum, removed ledger row, removed entry). 25 cases now, was 19. (3) E-014 recorded guard:gate:content while the real guard was gate:test — true before the fixture had a bundle, and now genuinely both. (4) The paired memory notes for E-001 and E-006 were left stale while effects.json was updated, in direct contradiction; both rewritten. (5) OUR_OWN_CURATION was exported, documented as forcing a decision, and consumed by nothing — the rule keyed on sourceType alone, which let an editorial source call itself "traditional" or "modern-japanese". Both are claims about the received canon and neither is ours to make; the rule is now a positive list and the constant is load-bearing. (6) A test asserting CLASSIFICATIONS.filter(isOurOwnCuration) equals OUR_OWN_CURATION was true by construction and could not fail; replaced with the literal complement. ONE FINDING RECORDED RATHER THAN FIXED: the workflow STATE MACHINE (assertTransition / canTransition) has no non-test call site, so criterion 4's "draft to review to verified to published to superseded" is not enforced as a sequence. It cannot be, in a file-based corpus: there is no previous status on disk to compare a new one against. What IS enforced is every per-status obligation — a reviewer is required from `verified` onward and forbidden before it, only published|superseded enter a bundle, and author must differ from reviewer. Sequence enforcement needs stored prior state and belongs to F-062 (editorial review workflow); the machine is built and tested here so F-062 inherits it rather than reinventing it. Recorded as an attested criterion rather than claimed.

features.title: Japanese colour atlas seed corpus
acceptance: Seed corpus published with 100 percent complete provenance and a named reviewer per entry
Contemporary palette systems: Quiet Neutrals, Indigo Studies, Forest and Mineral, Earth and Clay, Seasonal
Every palette has an anchor role and editorial provenance
Every source appears in the register in docs/content/licensing-and-provenance.md
No entry derives from a scraped or unlicensed dataset
features.notes: BLOCKED — not on engineering, on a person. The acceptance criterion is a corpus PUBLISHED with a named reviewer per entry. `verified`, `published` and `superseded` all require complete provenance AND author != reviewer, compared as roster ids against content/editors.json (ADR-0047). That roster holds exactly ONE identity, ed-001. No entry can reach `published` until a second real editorial identity exists, and inventing one would defeat the single check that makes review mean anything. OQ-5 (Japanese editorial reviewer — engagement model) is the open question that unblocks this, and it is a hiring or engagement decision, not a technical one. OQ-4 is closed: ~120 entries, depth over breadth. WHAT CAN PROCEED WITHOUT THE REVIEWER, and is worth doing first: `draft` and `review` statuses require no reviewer (workflow.ts REVIEWED_STATUSES), so entries can be authored and sourced now and promoted later. Before ANY entry can cite a source, real rows must be added to docs/content/licensing-and-provenance.md section 5 — with no registered sources every citing entry fails, which is the correct direction. ALSO OWED HERE, and easy to forget: F-013 has never run against real data. Its naming equivalence suite prints "Real corpus entries available: 0" and NOTHING re-runs it when entries land. A synthetic corpus is adversarial where a real one is clustered, so the recorded shortlist fractions (40.8% / 12.9% / 2.1%) will move.

attested.criterion: Output language is closest digital reference, never an assertion of identity; enforced by the claims lint

F-013 delivers the STRUCTURAL half and that half is gated here: limit < 3 throws and buildNamingIndex refuses fewer than 3 records, because a single answer is an identification (ADR-0031); and no field in NamingCandidate or NamingResult can be read as an identity claim, asserted as an exact key set with a decoy carrying an exact-match flag. features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: @irodora/color-naming — a Lab bucket index, a provable lower bound on ΔE00 to any box, an expanding search with a stopping rule, the ΔE00 ranking with a total comparator, the ADR-0048 similarity scale, and an adapter from a published corpus bundle. 59 tests here plus 4 in @irodora/corpus. NO CORPUS ENTRIES EXIST — F-012 is blocked on OQ-4/OQ-5 — so the suite runs on generated corpora and prints that it did. CRITERION 3 HOLDS: two-stage is byte-identical to brute force over 4,664 synthetic records x 120 adversarial queries, at four limits, at bucket steps 1/2/5/25/1e6, cross-checked against culori. MEASURED PRUNING, printed not claimed: n=45 examines 40.8%, n=416 12.9%, n=4203 2.1%. The plan warned the bound might examine ~100% at R1 sizes; it does not, and the fraction FALLS as the corpus grows. Asserted as a trend, never a threshold — a threshold at these sizes would flake and then get deleted. THE CORRECTNESS ARGUMENT IS THE FEATURE. A fixed radius — the design criterion 2 most naturally reads as — is wrong on 317 of 360 queries, first at n=45, because ΔE00 is not a metric and Lab distance does not bound it. Instead: a sound lower bound per bucket, visit in increasing bound, stop when the next cannot beat the k-th best. Correctness is then INDEPENDENT of bucket size, which the invariance test is what proves. The bound was built FIRST, out of plan order, because it was the cheapest moment to discover the algebra was wrong; four facts re-derived rather than cited, and 130k+ property samples concentrated where each could fail — plus a 200k-iteration decoy run where an unsound bound is caught and ours has zero violations. THREE THINGS TESTS FOUND THAT I HAD WRONG. (1) A property test disproved ADR-0048 on run 1: similarity is NOT strictly decreasing, because the curve is not injective in float64. The ADR now claims only monotone non-increasing — and this is an argument FOR the design, since sorting by similarity would tie where ΔE00 does not and reorder with input order. (2) The culori cross-check disagreed by 0.81 ΔE00 because culori lab is D50 and ours is D65; color-difference already calls it as lab65. A cross-check is only a check if both are asked the same question. (3) A bucket-box test assumed one bucket and got three: floor(-30/1000) is -1, so negatives land in the cell below zero. Correct behaviour, wrong expectation. A PLAN CORRECTION MADE BY typecheck IN UNDER A MINUTE: the plan specified a Color query and asserted no cycle. @irodora/color-core is the FACADE and already depends on color-naming, so depending back is a cycle by construction, and the corpus devDependency closed it again via core. The query is a Lab triple; provenance-aware wrapping belongs in the facade. The VersionBundle assignability guard moved into packages/corpus, which is the better home — the schema is that package’s contract to keep. AS A RESULT F-073 IS NOT DISCHARGED AND NOT NEEDED: the engine-to-non-engine edge does not exist rather than being contained. CRITERION 4 SHIPS HALF-GATED, declared as attested rather than discovered at the end. The structural half is enforced here — limit < 3 throws, an index of fewer than 3 records is refused, and the exact key sets of NamingCandidate and NamingResult are asserted with an exact-match-flag decoy so ADDING a field breaks the test. The lint half is F-025’s. DOCS CORRECTED: color-engine.md section 8 said "candidate retrieval from the corpus (spatially indexed for speed)" — defensible but the exact phrasing that invites the fixed radius, in a document the rules tell an implementer to read in full. It now states that retrieval is indexed and ranking cannot be, and carries the 317/360 measurement. E-003’s memory note said its consumers "do not exist yet"; that became false here and was rewritten.

features.title: Harmony engine
acceptance: Monochromatic, tonal, analogous, complementary, split, triadic, tetradic, neutral, near-neutral, warm/cool, value-contrast and chroma-contrast generators
All generation happens in OKLCh, not HSL
Editorial Japanese harmonies sourced from the corpus, kept distinct from geometric ones
Every generated colour passes gamut mapping before it is returned
features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: @irodora/color-harmony — all twelve FR-6 generators in OKLCh, every output gamut-mapped and reporting what that cost, the geometric/editorial split with attribution enforced both ways, and an adapter from a published corpus bundle. 33 tests. NO PALETTES EXIST — F-012 is blocked on OQ-4/OQ-5 — so the editorial suite runs on generated bundles and prints that it did. THE STUB WAS WRONG AGAINST ITS OWN ACCEPTANCE LIST: nine kinds where FR-6 requires twelve (missing near-neutral, warm-cool, value-contrast, chroma-contrast) AND it carried `editorial` as a KIND, which conflates two axes and makes criterion 3 unexpressible — an editorial harmony is a family, not a relationship. THE PLAN WAS ALSO WRONG, and is corrected in place: it said "an editorial harmony still stands in some relationship". Not in general — a curator assembling Quiet Neutrals is not obliged to have picked a triad, and labelling it afterwards would invent a geometric claim they never made. So `kind` is null for editorial. THE MEASUREMENT THAT JUSTIFIES THE WHOLE DESIGN. color-engine.md asserted that HSL hue rotation is perceptually inconsistent and never measured it. Over the hue circle a 30-degree HSL rotation moves the colour by ΔE00 5.0 to 35.9 — a 7.2x SPREAD. The same rotation in OKLCh ranges 9.7 to 14.5, a 1.5x spread. Asserted on the SPREAD rather than either end, because inconsistency is the claim; and OKLab is NOT asserted to be ΔE00-uniform, which would be its own over-claim. CRITERION 4 AND FR-6 PULL AGAINST EACH OTHER, AND ADR-0045 RESOLVES IT. Mapping changes a colour, so it could break the relationship just built. It does not for HUE — gamutMap holds L and h — measured here at 6.2e-5 degrees for a complementary pair and 5.3e-5 for a triad. It DOES for chroma, so chroma-contrast has a weaker tolerance and every colour reports wasGamutMapped and gamutDeltaE00. That makes E-012 a sharper link than it was: harmony depends on the PROPERTY ADR-0045 chose, not just on the function. ADR-0049: warm and cool are a stated convention anchored to the corpus taxonomy, because every other generator is derivable and this one is not — and if the engine picked its own anchors the product would contradict `taxonomy.temperature`. The ADR is blunt about the cost: two numbers cannot express a convention that varies by culture, and this product's subject is Japanese colour. PLANNED WITHOUT THE PLANNER SUBAGENT, recorded as a deviation: AGENTS.md recommends it, and it was used for F-011 and F-013 — both plans contained a factual error about this repository (F-013's asserted "no cycle" when color-core is the facade). Direct authorship after building both adjacent packages was the more reliable path here. Not a licence to skip planning: the plan exists and gate 0 enforced it.

features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: scripts/verify-claims.mjs inside gate 2, .harness/verification/claims.json holding the patterns as DATA, scripts/verify-claims-proof.mjs, and a clean fixture. Golden rule 11 is now a gate rather than a habit. THE PROBLEM THIS GATE HAS: the banned phrases must appear in this repository — ADR-0031 lists them, so do the governance doc, three skills and two rule files. A naive scan flags 18 files, most of them the policy. A blanket exemption for documents-discussing-the-policy would BE the gate, since every real claim in docs/ sits inside it. Answered with three exemption KINDS that are not interchangeable: policySource (an explicit file list, never a glob, 20 entries each with a reason), an inline claims-ok: marker scoped to ONE line and requiring a 12+ character reason, and `measured` requiring a link to a device-lab row. `measured` IS EMPTY and the count is printed every run — the device colour lab is F-063, and no number may exist without a row. FOUND ON ACTIVATION: the design system thesis was “soft chrome, exact colour”, a tagline asserting exactness in a product whose central commitment is that capture is an estimate. It meant the swatch carries no corner radius — rendering geometry, not accuracy — but a two-word thesis migrates into marketing faster than an identifier migrates into a field. Reworded to “unaltered colour”. Also corrected three “the true colour” comments in corpus/derive.ts to “specified”, which is more precise anyway. A FALSE POSITIVE I INTRODUCED AND FIXED BEFORE ACTIVATION: the actual-colour pattern had no determiner, so it fired on its own ADR-0052 (“covers actual colours” = real colours, ordinary English). Now requires the|its|their|your|a. PROVEN: 14 cases, each watched, baseline green either side — 12 red (one per construction plus a bare marker) and TWO green (a marker with a reason, and the clean fixture), with every red case also asserting the output NAMES the right construction. NOT DELIVERED, printed on every run: the provenance-conditional half of ADR-0031 §1. Deciding whether “measured” sits near an estimated value needs the render tree; it activates with F-017 and the table is already in claims.json.

features.title: Cross-theme salience hierarchy for the status tokens, and the APCA floor for dark error
acceptance: The salience rank of status.ok, status.warn and status.bad against each theme own ground is the same in both themes

The contrast gate asserts the rank, so it cannot drift back
features.notes: FOUND BY THE F-003 DESIGN AND COLOUR-SCIENCE REVIEWS. PRE-EXISTING — not introduced by F-003. TWO DRIVERS, ONE DECISION. (1) SALIENCE INVERSION: measured against each theme own background, the dark theme says caution is the loudest state and error the quietest, while the light theme says error is loudest by nearly 2x. A user toggling the theme gets an inverted status hierarchy. The cause is that the approved system holds the rank of OKLCh L constant across two grounds of OPPOSITE polarity, and L rank does not survive that flip — the invariant that makes the themes one system is rank of CONTRAST against own ground. (2) THE APCA FLOOR: dark.status.bad sits at APCA Lc -37.5 to -38.6 against its three declared surfaces — below the Lc 45 LARGE-text floor of 0.98G-4g — while WCAG reads 4.92 to 5.58 and passes. ADR-0044 classifies status.* as usage:text precisely because the product tints the label, so this is body copy below even the large-text floor in the DEFAULT theme. MEASURED AND INFEASIBLE SEPARATELY: holding status.ok and status.warn at their current values, NO value of status.bad reaches even Lc 40 while keeping CVD separation at or above 60 — the APCA floor and the separation minimum are in direct tension at the current lightness arrangement. A jointly feasible solution exists and was computed during F-003 — dark ok L0.67 C0.12 H158, warn L0.70 C0.14 H70, bad L0.82 C0.10 H18, worst separation 63.1, every token above Lc 45 — but it makes error the LIGHTEST token in the dark theme, which is exactly the salience re-arrangement in driver (1). That is a redesign larger than either defect and belongs to a person rather than to a gate-building task. Until it is decided, gate 9 prints the three pairings in a separate RED band on every run so they cannot be mistaken for the ordinary WCAG/APCA disagreements.

acceptance: border.strong reaches 3:1 against every surface it can sit on, under BOTH the linear and the encoded compositing model

features.notes: FOUND BY THE F-003 COLOUR-SCIENCE REVIEW. border.strong role is Outlined controls, which is a UI component boundary under WCAG 1.4.11 and therefore owes 3:1 — it is not the decorative-hairline exemption that covers border. MEASURED over its own declared grounds: dark 3.11:1 linear (worst ground surface.3) but only 1.41:1 encoded (over background); light 1.17:1 linear and 1.41:1 encoded (over surface.3). It fails under the encoded model in both themes, and the encoded model is what a browser and React Native actually draw. THE CONFLICT: reaching 3:1 needs roughly 53 percent alpha, which is a solid grey line, and the design system states a border is a translucent overlay and NEVER a solid grey because depth must read as lift rather than outline. So this is a design decision, not a value tweak — either the outline stops being the only thing identifying the control (a filled or tinted control state would remove the 1.4.11 obligation), or the never-a-solid-grey rule is amended. F-003 made the token VISIBLE rather than fixing it: it carries an uncheckedReason with these ratios in it, and the gate now fails any token that is covered by nothing and does not declare why.

features.title: The property-test gates are deterministic
acceptance: Every fast-check property runs from a recorded seed, so a failure is reproducible and a pass is not luck
No gate can go red for a reason unrelated to the change under test
A test whose tolerance is within a small factor of the true error bound states the measured margin
features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: all three acceptance criteria, and the third one turned out to be a real defect rather than a tidy-up. (1) SEEDS — 41 of 48 fc.assert calls ran unseeded across 8 files; every property in the repository now carries a distinct recorded seed, 56 in total, uniqueness asserted by a grep rather than by assumption. (2) TIMEOUTS — 30 CPU-bound properties inherited vitest's default 5000 ms because packages ran bare `vitest run` with no config at all. Twelve config files now set 120 s. Proven by FIVE consecutive full `turbo run test --force` runs, 25/25 tasks each, against three separately observed flakes beforehand (testing/PRNG at 7061, 6863 and 5299 ms; color-naming/bound at 5052 ms). (3) THE TOLERANCE WAS NOT A MARGIN PROBLEM, IT WAS WRONG — F-071 recorded oklab round-trip as failing once at 1.2477e-12 against 1e-12, "a 25 percent overshoot". Measured over 2,000,000 cases from that generator the worst error is 5.422e-8: a factor of 54,000, not 25 percent. It passed because 5,000 unseeded samples almost never reach the tail, and seeding it WITHOUT measuring first would have frozen that luck in permanently. The cause is conditioning, not a defect: oklabToXyz cubes LMS-prime and xyzToOklab cube-roots it back, and d/dx x^(1/3) diverges at zero — the worst case has LMS-prime = [0.203, -3.7e-5, -0.488], whose cubes span a ratio of 2.3e12. Settled by ADR-0052: the claim splits into a measured 1e-6 over the full declared range (18x margin) and 1e-12 where LMS is well conditioned (21x margin), each stating its measured worst case and sample size. Real colours are unaffected — the stratified sRGB test holds at 1e-14 and in-gamut probes measure 2.78e-16. DISCRIMINATION PROVEN, not assumed: a 1e-5 perturbation of XYZ_TO_LMS_OKLAB[0][0] turns BOTH new seeded properties red, so the seeds catch a real engine change rather than having narrowed coverage to nothing. A DEFECT I INTRODUCED AND CAUGHT: the batch script that rewrote the configs reported "updated 5 existing" having updated 2 — three files used a single-line body the regex missed, and were left importing a helper they never called. Found by the contrast mutation proof, whose BASELINE went to exit 2. Recorded as memory/lessons/a-batch-edit-that-reports-its-own-success-is-not-evidence.md. ALSO REJECTED AND RECORDED: a root vitest.shared.ts, which every package tsconfig refuses with TS6059 because rootDir is the package and *.config.ts is deliberately included; and moving it into @irodora/testing, which would make every package's config fail to LOAD whenever that package's build broke. The timeout is therefore repeated in 12 files with the reasoning in each. NOT DONE: nothing. All three criteria are met and each was watched to fail.

features.title: Gate 0 sees a CI step that is conditioned out
acceptance: An active gate whose CI step carries an `if:` fails gate 0, naming the gate
verify-gate-mirror.mjs proves that check by adding a condition to a real step and watching gate 0 go red
Every remaining conditional step for an active gate is either unconditional or justified in gates.json
features.notes: DONE. Gate 0 compared whole run-commands and NEVER READ `if:`, so a gate could read active, have a step, pass the mirror check, and never once execute. FOUND SEVEN OF ELEVEN ACTIVE GATES CONDITIONED OUT: typecheck, lint, format, test and build on hashFiles(pnpm-lock.yaml); color-golden on a package.json; and — the worst — cvd on hashFiles(packages/cvd-engine/dist), A BUILD OUTPUT, so a build that produced nothing would have silently skipped the gate rather than failing. None was skipping yet; all seven were one rename away, with nothing to report it. All seven now unconditional: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` already fails the job when the lockfile is missing, so the hashFiles guards protected nothing that was not already protected. Also removed the same condition from the Set up pnpm, Install and dependency-audit steps. THE ESCAPE HATCH: a conditional step is not always wrong — a push-only benchmark is a cadence choice — so gates.json may declare ciCondition {condition, why}, with why required at 20+ characters for the same reason F-025 requires a reason on claims-ok: an exemption nobody had to justify is a way to turn a blocking gate off. PROVEN IN ALL THREE DIRECTIONS, by hand and recorded: declared + real reason stays GREEN (the hatch works, which matters because an untested escape hatch is a wall for whoever first needs it); declared + trivial reason goes RED; declared condition not matching the workflow goes RED, because a stale declaration reads as reviewed while describing something no longer there. verify-gate-mirror.mjs now runs 22 cases rather than 11: it REMOVES each active gate step and, separately, CONDITIONS IT OUT with `if: false` while leaving the run: in place — the quiet failure the loud one hides. SCOPE, stated rather than left to be wondered about: the check applies to ACTIVE gates only. Gate 12 (perf) is pending and keeps its push-only condition; blocking a pending gate from being staged conditionally would make the check hostile to its own purpose.

features.title: Engine purity follows @irodora/* dependency edges
acceptance: A package outside the engine zone that an engine package depends on is held to the same platform-API and runtime-dependency rules, transitively
scripts/verify-engine-purity.mjs --prove plants exactly that violation and watches the check fail
features.notes: DONE. The engine zone is now a GRAPH rather than a naming convention. verify-engine-purity.mjs scoped itself by package NAME (color-* and cvd-engine) and treated every @irodora/* specifier inside those as allowed WITHOUT FOLLOWING THE EDGE — so an engine package could depend on a workspace package that imports node:fs, or that declares a third-party runtime dependency, and every gate stayed green while NFR-3 was broken. A transitive node:fs breaks byte-identical output in Node, the browser and React Native exactly as directly as a local one. The zone is now the transitive closure of @irodora/* dependency edges from the declared roots, and every member is held to both existing rules. NOTHING WAS VIOLATING IT: today the closure equals the roots exactly, and the check SAYS SO on every run rather than printing a bare count — a count cannot distinguish "no transitive packages" from "did not look". That is a fact about this commit, not a property anyone was maintaining: F-011 already hit the hazard once, expecting color-naming to import @irodora/corpus, and handled it by hand with a portability override plus boundary guard #11. One package, not a rule. PROVEN: --prove now runs three planted violations rather than two. The new one is the case the old check COULD NOT SEE — color-spaces gains a dependency on @irodora/recommendation, which is not a root, and that package src gains a node:fs import. Caught, with the clean baseline asserted first and last, and every fixture verified removed. A failure message now NAMES THE EDGE that pulled a package in, so it reads as "corpus is in the zone via @irodora/color-naming" rather than leaving someone to ask why corpus is an engine package. THE COST, stated rather than discovered: a package pulled into the zone inherits the whole constraint set, so wanting an engine package to use a helper that reads a file is now a design decision rather than an accident.
